recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say why a/(1 − r) cannot be used straight away, and what you do instead.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by the ratio 1/2 and subtract
steps.margin_note: First mark. The shift-and-subtract is the method mark. Line the powers of 2 up under each other before subtracting, or the differences come out wrong.
steps.memory_tip: Numerators in A.P. over denominators in G.P.: multiply by the ratio and subtract.
lines: The numerators 1, 2, 3, 4, … are in A.P. and the denominators are in G.P. of ratio 1/2

recall.must_convey: That this is not a G.P., so S is multiplied by the ratio 1/2 and subtracted term by term.
accept: this is not a geometric series so multiply by half and subtract
the numerators are in A P and the denominators in G P
shift by one place and subtract so the numerators become one
half tho multiply chesi subtract cheyyali
use the S minus r S method

steps.why: The terms are not in G.P., so a/(1 − r) cannot be applied to the series as it stands. Shifting by one place and subtracting makes every numerator difference equal to 1, and what is left IS a geometric series.
common_mistakes: Treating the series as a G.P. with r = 1/2 and giving 2.
Multiplying by 2 instead of by the ratio 1/2, which does not line the terms up.

steps.label: Sum the geometric series that is left
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The last move — multiplying by 2 — is the one most often missed. What the subtraction gives is S/2, not S.
steps.memory_tip: After the subtraction you are holding half of S, so double it at the end.
lines: This is a G.P. with a = 1 and r = 1/2, and |r| < 1, so

recall.must_convey: That half of S is a G.P. summing to 2, so S = 4.
accept: what is left is a G P with first term one and ratio half
half of S is two so S is four
one over one minus half gives two
S by two equals two, so S four vasthundi

steps.why: The subtraction leaves half of S equal to a plain geometric series of first term 1 and ratio 1/2, which sums to 2, so S = 4. Adding the first five terms already gives 1 + 1 + 0.75 + 0.5 + 0.3125 = 3.5625, so 4 is the right size.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the left side is (1/2)S and giving 2 as the final answer.
Dropping the leading 1 when writing out the series that is left.
